o: Define malware and identify common types.
Explain phishing and other social engineering threats.
Describe realistic consequences of a compromised device.
c: Malware is software designed to harm, disrupt or gain unauthorised access to systems. Different malware types have different behaviours.
A trojan disguises itself as legitimate software; worms replicate to spread; ransomware may encrypt files and demand payment.
Attackers deceive people into sharing information or taking an unsafe action. A phishing message impersonates a trusted organisation.
Unexpected links, urgency and requests for account details are warning signs. Know the threat and explain why sharing credentials is dangerous.

m.title: Suspicious school email
m.q: A pupil receives a message pretending to be school IT and asking for login details via a link. Explain the threat and TWO possible consequences. [4 marks]
st: The sender pretends to be a trusted school service.
This is phishing/social engineering [1]: the pupil is directed to a fake page or asked for details [1].
The attacker may capture login credentials [1] and gain unauthorised access to the pupil's account [1].
Name the threat, describe the deception and link data theft to access.

w: A pupil downloads an apparently harmless game that secretly installs malicious software. Explain the threat and two possible effects. [4 marks]
It is a trojan [1] disguised as legitimate software [1]. It could steal personal data [1] or damage/delete files [1].
A school finds files have been encrypted and an attacker demands money. Explain this threat and its effect. [4 marks]
Ransomware is malicious software [1] that encrypts/locks files [1]. Users cannot access the files [1] and an attacker demands payment for restoration [1].
A fake text claims a student's account will close unless they enter a password. Explain why this is social engineering. [4 marks]
It impersonates a trusted service [1] and creates urgency [1], manipulating the victim [1] into disclosing account credentials [1].
wSteps: Identify what makes this download deceptive.
The hidden malware can steal data or corrupt files [2].
It is a trojan [1] disguised as legitimate software [1]. It could steal personal data [1] or damage/delete files [1].
Follow from malware type to what happens to files.
Files are inaccessible and payment is demanded [2].
Ransomware is malicious software [1] that encrypts/locks files [1]. Users cannot access the files [1] and an attacker demands payment for restoration [1].
Fake authority and urgency are signs of deception [2].
The person is manipulated to disclose credentials [2].
It impersonates a trusted service [1] and creates urgency [1], manipulating the victim [1] into disclosing account credentials [1].

k.q: Create a safe training warning based on a simulated suspicious-message flag. Do not open links or use real accounts.
k.code:
suspicious = 1
if suspicious > 0 then
    print("Report the message")
else
    print("Follow normal checks")
endif
p: Add print("Never share login details") after the decision.
k.a:
For 1: Report the message. For 0: Follow normal checks.

e:
Define phishing. [2 marks]

Source: Adapted from your Paper 1 revision booklet, 1.4.1.
Deceptive messages impersonate a trusted source [1] to trick users into revealing personal data/credentials [1].

Explain how ransomware could disrupt a school. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style question, not a past-paper original.
Ransomware infects a device [1] and encrypts or locks files [1]. Teachers/pupils cannot access their work [1] and learning/administration may be disrupted [1].

Explain malware and social engineering threats, giving three specific consequences. [6 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style question, not a past-paper original.

Malware is malicious software [1] that can steal data or corrupt files [1]. Social engineering deceives people [1] to reveal information [1]. Examples of consequences: unauthorised access [1] and lost/unavailable data [1].
v: Malicious software that harms or compromises systems.
Malware able to replicate and spread to other systems.
Malware that can lock or encrypt data and demand payment.
Manipulating people to reveal information or take risky actions.
Deceptive messages seeking personal or account information.
Redirecting users to a fraudulent website.
x: A trojan is always harmless because it looks like legitimate software.
r: State one benefit of agreed networking standards. [1 mark]
They allow equipment/software from different manufacturers to communicate/interoperate [1].
State one function of SMTP. [1 mark]
Sends email between clients/servers or mail servers [1].
State one role of an IP address. [1 mark]
Identifies a network destination/used for routing [1].
A business replaces copper cable with fibre for a long link. Explain one advantage and one limitation. [4 marks]
Fibre carries light [1] at high rates/long distances [1]. It can cost more to buy/install [1], making initial deployment more expensive [1].
